name: Tastes That Took Over the World
description: Bread, tea, coffee, chocolate, pizza and cola: how the foods and drinks of one place ended up on every table.

checkpoints.name: The first kitchens
checkpoints.note: Farmers learned to bake bread, ferment grain and fruit into beer and wine, and turn milk into cheese. Rice was grown in flooded fields of Asia, cacao was drunk in Mesoamerica, and noodles were made in northern China.

checkpoints.name: Trade and taste
checkpoints.note: Tea became a drink of China, and Romans fermented fish into a sauce sold across the Mediterranean. Japanese cooks developed fermented rice dishes that led to sushi.

checkpoints.name: Spirits and pasta
checkpoints.note: Kimchi, pasta and coffee took shape in Korea, Italy and Arabia, and distillers made strong drinks. After 1492 the Columbian exchange carried maize and potatoes from the Americas to the Old World, and sugar grew into a mass commodity. Curry took shape as spices met local cooking in India.

checkpoints.name: Factories and fizz
checkpoints.note: Pizza grew in Naples and pharmacists in the United States created drinks that were sold as cures. Bottling, railways and cheaper sugar gave them a mass market in towns and cities.

checkpoints.name: The fast food age
checkpoints.note: Hamburgers, instant noodles and cola travelled with chains, ships and advertising, and Taiwan's bubble tea joined them near the end, carried by migrants and the internet.
